_comment: P1-85, third slice. Not a new defect -- a MUTATION SURVIVOR. mutation/mutate_p185.py mutant 6 narrows the pre-merge blank-leader refusal to the create path and the whole suite stays green, because a second check after the merge catches the edit case. Two rules for one question, so neither is load-bearing and neither can be tested. The suite is GREEN right now; this ticket must keep it green and make that mutant die.

tickets.title: One rule decides whether a group's leader is acceptable
tickets.defect:
`ApplyGroupRequest` now answers "is this leader acceptable?" in two places:

* under `_lock`, before the clone: `if (leaderKeyPresent && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(leader))`
* after `PopulateObject`: `if (leaderKeyInNormalized && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(grp.LeaderAccountName))`

Both refuse, with the same message and the same event type. Mutation testing found the consequence: `mutate_p185.py` mutant 6 narrows the FIRST check to the create path only -- which is exactly the incomplete fix the review panel flagged on the previous landing -- and the entire suite stays green, because the second check silently covers for it.

A rule stated twice cannot be tested, because neither statement is load-bearing on its own. And the two are not even equivalent: the first reads the RAW REQUEST through `ReqStr`, the second reads the MERGED OBJECT. Only the second sees what was actually about to be stored.
tickets.spec:
Reduce it to one rule, in `addons/TradeCopierEngine.cs`, `ApplyGroupRequest` only.

A. DELETE the `leaderKeyPresent && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(leader)` branch under the lock, and the `leaderKeyPresent` local that exists only to feed it. What stays under the lock is the create-path check -- `isNew && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(leader)` -- because a new group must not be constructed at all without a leader. Widen its reason to cover blank as well as absent, since `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` already covers both and the message currently says only "missing".

B. Make the post-merge check UNCONDITIONAL: refuse whenever `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(grp.LeaderAccountName)` after the merge, whatever the request did or did not name. Drop the `leaderKeyInNormalized` guard.

That is the stronger invariant and the one worth stating: **no group with a blank leader is ever stored**, by any route. The conditional version only asked whether THIS request mentioned the leader, which is a question about the request rather than about the group.

C. Say on the check that it is the single place this is decided, and that it runs on the clone -- so a refusal here leaves the stored group untouched.

WHAT NOT TO DO:
* Do NOT weaken either behaviour. An edit that does not mention the leader must still be accepted and must keep the stored leader; an edit that names it blank must still be refused; a new group with no leader must still be refused. There is a test for each.
* Do NOT move the refusal after `UpsertGroup`. It must run on the clone, before anything is stored.
* Do NOT touch `ApplyRelationshipRequest`. There the account names are the lookup key, refused at the top, and now covered by their own test.
* Do NOT change the load path or `NormalizeRequest`.
tickets.context:
THE SUITE IS GREEN AT 1177/0. This is a simplification, not a fix: no acceptance test is red, and `expect_green` is deliberately empty because there is nothing red to go green. The evidence that it worked is the MUTATION BATTERY, not the suite -- `mutation/mutate_p185.py` mutant 6 must go from SURVIVED to KILLED, and every other mutant in that battery must stay killed.

WHY THE REDUNDANCY IS NOT FREE. It is the same shape as `P?-64` (two owners of the copier config path) and `R4` in docs/CONFIG_DEFAULTS.md (two names for one cap): whichever copy the next reader finds is the one they will edit, and the other keeps its old behaviour. Here it also made a genuine review finding untestable.

ASCII only. C# 8.0 / .NET Framework 4.8 and a net8.0 test build. `CopierLog` reaches another component, so it must not be called while holding `_lock`.
